correctness.rationale: Using the affine-invariant definition L_K^(2d)=det(A(K))/vol(K)^2, Cartesian products give block-diagonal covariance and exact multiplicativity. For an l1-sum, beta-integral fiber formulas give the volume p!q!/d! times the product volume and covariance factors (p+1)(p+2)/((d+1)(d+2)) and its q-analogue, yielding C_{p,q}. The quotient C_{p+1,q-1}/C_{p,q}=h(p+1)/h(q) with h(x)=(1+1/x)(1+2/x)^x reduces the coefficient maximum to a one-dimensional split. The strict logarithmic lower bound log(1+t)>2t/(2+t) proves C_{p,q}<=1, with equality only in dimension two. Induction on the Hanner recursion gives the stated extrema and rigidity.
risks: The finite checker only diagnoses the exact recursion over bounded dimensions; it is not used as the proof.

value.rationale: Hanner polytopes are a canonical recursively generated family central to the symmetric Mahler problem, while the cube is the conjectured sharp maximizer for the centrally symmetric isotropic problem. Establishing the exact cube upper endpoint on the full Hanner class is therefore a motivated benchmark. The simultaneous cross-polytope lower endpoint, equality rigidity, and exact nodewise loss coefficient make the result structural rather than a one-off calculation.
risks: The result is class-specific and does not resolve the general centrally symmetric strong isotropic conjecture.
